clue.text: Bell and transmission for bicycle manufactured in the meadow ?

parts.note: the old song 'Daisy Bell' is about a bicycle built for two, so Bell's first name is Daisy
a bicycle's drive is carried from pedals to wheel by its chain

explanation.surface: A bicycle's bell and gears seem to be made out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bell' looks like the bicycle's bell, but it is Daisy Bell of the song 'Daisy, Daisy ... a bicycle made for two'. The definition describes the thing children make from flowers in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of little flowers threaded together stem to stem is made by children sitting in grassy fields.

clue.text: Army attitude ?

parts.note: read 'Army' as arm-y, a posture all about the arms: hands on hips, elbows out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' suggests soldiers, but it is a made-up adjective, 'of the arms', and the attitude is a stance with hands on hips and elbows bent outwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing with hands on hips and elbows pointing out is a pose defined entirely by how the arms are held.

clue.text: There are no outstanding accounts of these colonists

definitions.text: There are no outstanding accounts of these
definitions.meaning: people who pay off their bills leave no debts unpaid
people who make a home in a new land

explanation.surface: No surviving records exist of some early pioneers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding accounts' reads as notable stories about the colonists, but it means unpaid bills: those who settle up leave none.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb to settle: to pay off a debt, and to make a new home in an unoccupied territory.

clue.text: Relative sought by the railway traveller?

definitions.meaning: a person related to you by blood or marriage
a passenger changing trains looks for the onward train that links with the first

explanation.surface: A train passenger is out looking for a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A family member is one of your kin, and a train timed to meet another lets a passenger change to it.

clue.text: High honour to Harry the comic salt

parts.note: in card games the ace is the top card and, in bridge, one of the honours
Harry Tate was a popular British music-hall comedian of the early twentieth century

explanation.surface: Top recognition is awarded to a comedian named Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Tate was a famous British music-hall comedian. 'Salt' is meant in the chemical sense, a compound formed from an acid.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, a compound of acetic acid with a metal is a salt of that acid.

clue.text: It's hard to be hit on the head

definitions.text: It's hard to be hit on the head

parts.words: It's hard to be hit on the head
parts.note: a hard metal spike struck on its flat top with a hammer, recalling the phrase about hitting it right on the head

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like sympathy for someone struck on the head; it describes a hard metal fastener that is hammered on its head, and the idiom for getting something exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: This metal fastener is driven in by hammer blows on its flat top, its head.

clue.text: An option on the services of a keeper

definitions.meaning: a fee paid in advance to reserve someone's work when it is wanted
a servant or attendant who keeps and looks after something, as an old family servant does

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper's services are secured on a provisional deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an advance fee securing a lawyer's work and a long-serving household servant.

clue.text: Food supplier to a former railway company — all right ?

parts.note: something former is in the past
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A caterer to an old railway firm asks if everything is in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker of pies and tarts provides food.

clue.text: An infrequent visitor to a girl

parts.note: angels' visits are proverbially few and far between

explanation.surface: A girl receives a visit only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'like angels' visits, few and far between' makes an angel the infrequent visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: The length of many lengths of course

definitions.meaning: how far it is from one point to another
on a racecourse, a winning margin of over thirty lengths is given this name

explanation.surface: How long a racehorse's huge winning margin is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally', but it is the racecourse: a horse winning by over thirty lengths wins by this margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A length between two points is the space between them, and racing uses the same word for a huge margin of victory.

clue.text: To the left they were classically indulgent

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
erant is Latin, the classical language, for 'they were'

explanation.surface: Politicians on the left were once known for being easy-going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classically' signals Latin: ERANT is 'they were'. 'The left' sounds political but just gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone indulgent puts up with the faults and wishes of others, which is to be forbearing.

clue.text: Lucy's spring bird ?

definitions.meaning: Wordsworth's Lucy 'dwelt among the untrodden ways / Beside the springs of' this English river
a small pigeon, a symbol of peace

explanation.surface: A girl called Lucy has a bird that appears in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but it is a water source: Wordsworth's Lucy lived beside the springs of the river of this name in Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the river named in Wordsworth's Lucy poem and a pigeon-like bird.

clue.text: Where the little ladies of China take their tea ?

definitions.text: Where the little ladies of China take their tea ?

parts.words: Where the little ladies of China take their tea
parts.note: the little ladies are porcelain figures, china rather than Chinese, sitting down to a pretend tea in their miniature home

explanation.walkthrough: 'China' with a capital looks like the country, but it is porcelain: the little ladies are china toys, and their home is a miniature house.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy house in miniature is where small figures are set out for play tea parties.

clue.text: "Be sure that your umbrella is upside down" to make a small profit?

definitions.text: "Be sure that your umbrella is upside down" to make a small profit?

parts.words: Be sure that your umbrella is upside down
parts.note: an inverted umbrella would collect coins as they fall, a picture of grabbing small sums

explanation.walkthrough: The advice pictures an umbrella turned over to catch falling coins; the word describes cheap goods made only to grab small sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy goods produced to sell quickly for small sums are designed to scoop up coins from buyers.

clue.text: Sonny Boy was so divine!

parts.note: the Al Jolson song tells Sonny Boy he came from above, a gift from the angels

explanation.walkthrough: Al Jolson's 1928 song 'Sonny Boy' says the child was sent from above; the phrase also means providentially welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arriving as if a gift from God is described as coming down from above.

clue.text: Court dress in action

parts.note: a court of law, so court suggests law
a suit is a set of clothes

explanation.surface: Formal clothes worn in action in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' is the legal sense, a case brought in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a case brought before a court by one party against another.

clue.text: Being a climber, a Baker Street visitor slept at this lodge

definitions.meaning: a climbing plant with hanging lilac flowers

definitions.text: a Baker Street visitor slept at this lodge
definitions.meaning: Holmes of Baker Street visits the lodge of this name in a Conan Doyle story

explanation.surface: A mountaineer who called on Holmes spent the night at a lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherlock Holmes lived at Baker Street; one of his adventures is set at a lodge named after this climbing plant with hanging lilac flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a climbing plant, and also the name of the lodge in a Conan Doyle Holmes story.

clue.text: A friend comes to the ruins of Rome in Sicily

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: ruins suggests Rome broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A companion visits the ancient ruins of Rome on the way to Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ruins of' signals an anagram: ROME becomes ERMO. 'Comes to' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of the island of Sicily.

clue.text: He takes turn at cooking a tuber

indicators.note: something cooking is being prepared and changed, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man takes his turn preparing a potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' is the anagram signal on HE plus TURN AT; 'takes' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The pignut plant has an edible underground tuber, eaten like a nut.

clue.text: In half of France many find it prevalent

parts.note: en is the French for 'in', as 'of France' directs
demi is the French for 'half', as 'of France' directs
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: In half of France, many people discover something widespread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of France' says to put 'in' and 'half' into French, EN and DEMI; C is Roman 100, a crossword stand-in for 'many'. 'Find it' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease regularly found among a people or region is widespread there.

clue.text: Can use nets craftily to get food

indicators.note: doing something craftily is doing it cunningly, so these letters are cunningly reworked

explanation.surface: A fisherman can cast nets skilfully to catch a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craftily' is the anagram signal on CAN USE NETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment is what keeps a body going, i.e. what you eat.

clue.text: Torture that leads to ruin

definitions.meaning: an instrument that stretches the body to inflict pain
the phrase 'go to ... and ruin' means fall into decay

explanation.surface: Cruelty that ends in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the stretching frame used for torture and the word paired with 'ruin' in the idiom for neglect and decay.

clue.text: That handkerchief … Thou gav'st to ——" (Othello)

parts.note: Othello accuses Desdemona of giving his handkerchief to his lieutenant

explanation.walkthrough: In Othello, Act 5, Othello says 'That handkerchief which I so lov'd and gave thee / Thou gav'st to' his lieutenant, whom Iago has framed.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank is filled by the name of Othello's lieutenant, whom he wrongly suspects of an affair with Desdemona.

clue.text: A far from rare Shakespearian mistress

definitions.meaning: meat that is far from rare has been cooked too long
Mistress ... is the bawd in Measure for Measure

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine who is anything but unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' suggests uncommon, but it is the steak sense: underdone. Mistress Overdone runs a brothel in Measure for Measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked too long is the opposite of bloody, and it is the surname of the bawd in Measure for Measure.

clue.text: The tent-maker

parts.note: Khayyam, the Persian poet of the Rubaiyat, means tent-maker, after his family trade

explanation.walkthrough: The Persian poet of the Rubaiyat bore the surname Khayyam, meaning tent-maker; the answer is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet known by the epithet of tent-maker had this as his first name.

clue.text: Quality that will get you the earth!

definitions.text: Quality that will get you the earth!

parts.words: Quality that will get you the earth
parts.note: the Sermon on the Mount promises that the humble shall inherit the earth

explanation.walkthrough: The Beatitudes say 'Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth', so the virtue named wins the whole world.
explanation.definitionFit: Humble gentleness is the virtue the Beatitudes say will be rewarded with the world.

clue.text: The way the American soldier runs back to mother is a disgrace!

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: running back means the soldier's letters are read from the end

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A US soldier fleeing home to his mother brings shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs back' reverses the soldier; 'the way' is the street abbreviation, and 'to' just links. The surface's deserter fleeing home disgraces himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of shame attaches to someone in disgrace.

clue.text: Changing in a trice to Gunga Din perhaps

indicators.note: changing letters around rearranges them, so the words that follow are reshuffled

explanation.surface: In an instant someone switches to reciting Kipling's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' is the anagram signal on IN A TRICE TO. Kipling's 'Gunga Din' is a poem often learned by heart and performed.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem performed aloud from memory is an example, and Kipling's ballad was a favourite party piece.
